record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.context_brief: Common explanation of F2 rise and forward jets
record.original_question: Why does F2 rise at small x? In particular, can one obtain a single QCD description that explains both the observed rise of F2 and the measured forward-jet cross-section in the region where DGLAP-based models fall below the data and BFKL-like dynamics may contribute?

evidence.quote: Forward Jet Production:8 Why does F2 rise?

The rise of F2 at small x is mirrored by the rise of the measured forward jet cross-section which is not described by the DGLAP-based models. A consistent description of the F2 and forward-jet data represents a considerable challenge to our understanding of QCD.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider deep inelastic electron–proton scattering at high center-of-mass energy, with photon virtuality $Q^2$ and Bjorken variable $x$. In perturbative QCD, two complementary resummation frameworks are available: the DGLAP equations, which resum logarithms of $Q^2$ via collinear parton evolution, and the BFKL equation, which resums logarithms of $1/x$ in the high-energy (Regge) limit.

Two observables probe small-$x$ QCD dynamics:

(i) the proton structure function $F_2(x,Q^2)$, which exhibits a steep rise as $x \to 0$ at fixed $Q^2$;

(ii) the forward-jet cross section in DIS, namely the cross section for producing a hadronic jet at small angle to the proton beam with transverse momentum $k_T^2 \sim Q^2$ and longitudinal momentum fraction $x_{\text{jet}} \gg x$, measured differentially in $x$ (and, more refinedly, triple-differentially in $x$, $k_T^2$, and $Q^2$).

Standard DGLAP-based parton-shower predictions, while accommodating $F_2$ through fitted parton densities, systematically fall below the measured forward-jet cross section in the region $x \ll x_{\text{jet}}$, $k_T^2 \approx Q^2$, where small-$x$ (BFKL-type) dynamics is expected to be enhanced.

Problem. Provide a single, theoretically consistent perturbative QCD description—e.g., a unified evolution scheme, an unintegrated parton distribution framework, or a resummation interpolating between DGLAP and BFKL—that simultaneously reproduces:
(a) the observed rise of $F_2(x,Q^2)$ at small $x$ over the measured range of $Q^2$, and
(b) the measured forward-jet cross section (including its differential distributions) in the small-$x$ region where DGLAP shower models undershoot the data.

Determine whether such a unified description exists, and if so, identify the dynamical ingredients (e.g., $\ln(1/x)$ resummation, next-to-leading BFKL corrections, $k_T$-factorization, saturation effects) that are required.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has made substantial progress: NLL-BFKL with renormalization-group improvement describes the triple-differential forward-jet cross sections at HERA while standard NLO DGLAP and LL-BFKL fail; color-dipole and $k_T$-factorization / CCFM-type frameworks (also saturation-improved dipole models) describe both the $F_2$ rise and forward-jet data reasonably well. A fully unified, first-principles description merging DGLAP and BFKL across all kinematics is, however, not yet established, so the question is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Next-to-leading BFKL phenomenology of forward-jet cross sections at HERA
status_evidence.snippet: NLL-BFKL with RG-improved kernel describes triple-differential forward-jet cross sections, while NLO DGLAP and LL-BFKL fail in the whole kinematic range.
status_evidence.claim: NLL-BFKL resummation provides a successful description of HERA forward-jet data where DGLAP-based approaches fail.

status_evidence.title: Forward Jet Production in Deep Inelastic Scattering at HERA (H1)
status_evidence.snippet: Excess of forward jets at small x is not reproduced by DGLAP-based parton shower models; the colour-dipole model gives a reasonable description.
status_evidence.claim: DGLAP shower models underpredict the forward-jet cross section, whereas dipole/BFKL-motivated approaches do better.

status_evidence.title: Color dipole cross section in the DGLAP improved saturation model
status_evidence.snippet: DGLAP-improved saturation/dipole model describes the small-x rise of F2 across a broad kinematic range.
status_evidence.claim: Saturation/dipole frameworks consistently describe the F2 rise at small x.
